title: From DNA to Protein
production_path_basis: The full information-flow explanation must remain understandable without narration or music.
central_message: Cells preserve and transform sequence information through transcription, RNA processing, export, and translation into an amino-acid sequence.
takeaway: A traceable nucleotide sequence can become an amino-acid sequence, but real gene expression and protein maturation are richer than a linear cartoon.
platform: website showcase and bundled desktop example
scientific_depth: introductory eukaryotic transcription directionality, complementary RNA, processing/export, codon translation, stop signaling, and folding boundaries
visual_direction: dark multiscale spatial journey with large high-contrast sans-serif labels and stable colors for gene, DNA, RNA, pore, ribosome, peptide, and schematic protein
pacing: cell entry, nucleus and gene approach, sequence tape, transcription, pore export, translation, folding boundary, synthesis
constraints: separate nuclear processing from cytoplasmic translation
identify stop as a signal rather than an amino acid
do not present the four-residue teaching chain as a realistic protein or structure prediction
success_criteria: DNA template and mRNA are exactly complementary
codons map to Met-Pro-Lys-Gly followed by Stop
cell, nucleus, gene, and sequence contexts remain explicit
RNA assembly, intron removal, exon joining, and nuclear-pore export are visibly staged
translation repeats codon highlight, tRNA arrival, amino-acid delivery, and ribosome movement
folding limitations appear before the final synthesis
